rows.reconciliation: page 42, the row `GRAND TOTAL`: interest 6,338,637.0 vs printed 6,338,637.0 ; principal 22,140,229.0 vs printed 22,140,229.0
rows.read_by: claude-opus-5 reading the text layer of pp.40-41 un-mirrored and transposed, and of p.42 with its measured one-row figure offset; every page also rendered and read by eye
rows.proof: TOWN OF LUNENBURG DEBT REPAYMENT SCHEDULE AS OF JUNE 30 2014, pages 40, 41 and 42. One table across three pages: fourteen debt issues, each with a PRINCIPAL, an INTEREST and a group TOTAL row, running FY2015-FY2047 plus a TOTAL column. PAGES 40 AND 41 are written vertically and MIRRORED, like the trust pages: reverse each word, flip x, and the page transposes, so a constant-y band is a FISCAL YEAR and a constant-x run is a debt line. PAGE 42 is printed the ordinary way but its FIGURE columns sit one row pitch (11.2pt) BELOW the labels they belong to. That offset is measured, not assumed: at +11.2 the TOTAL column reproduces the sum of pages 40 and 41 for 37 of 41 rows, and at 0 or -11.2 almost nothing ties. WHAT CLOSES. Principal + interest = the group total for every one of the 197 (issue, year) cells where the document prints all three. The year-by-year schedule sums to the printed GRAND TOTAL EXACTLY, to the dollar, for both principal ($22,140,229) and interest ($6,338,637). GRAND TOTAL PRINCIPAL + GRAND TOTAL INTEREST = TOTAL DEBT in all 33 years. WHAT DOES NOT, AND WHY. The page prints WHOLE DOLLARS over figures carrying cents, so a column of rounded addends need not sum to its own rounded total: four row sums are out by exactly one dollar and never more. Every one of the four is an INTEREST row or a total containing interest; no principal figure drifts anywhere, which is what a cents-rounding artefact looks like and is why a $1 tolerance is carried here rather than a misread being suspected. TWO CELLS ARE DOCUMENT DEFECTS and are attested below rather than reconciled. Together they are $1,040,704, which is exactly the amount by which the per-year TOTAL rows fall short of the printed GRAND TOTAL -- so once both are accounted for the whole table ties to the dollar.
